cur:manuscripts-otto-iii-entry-jerusalem.summary: In this black-and-white reproduction from a 1912 history of painting, Christ rides a donkey along a path beneath palm trees, while below crowds spread garments and branches before him. Although the colour is lost, the dynamic Reichenau composition remains clear.
facts: The Gospels of Otto III has 276 leaves, twelve canon tables, a double-page portrait of the emperor, four evangelist portraits and 29 full-page miniatures of New Testament scenes; it was produced at Reichenau around 1000.
Its original cover still holds a 10th-century Byzantine ivory of the Dormition of the Virgin.
cur:manuscripts-otto-iii-entry-jerusalem.notes: Only a 1912 black-and-white reproduction is available on Commons.

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: At the right, the haloed Christ stands and gestures toward two crowned rulers who sit on a bench and speak against him, with an attendant behind them. The verse above reads 'Princes also did sit and speak against me: but thy servant did meditate in thy statutes'.
facts: Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature. The haloed standing figure is identified as Christ following the manuscript's Christological reading.

wga:m/master/yunk_en/00cross.summary: Carved in high relief on the outside wall of Romsey Abbey, this large stone Christ stands upright on the cross with head erect and arms stretched straight out, not hanging in suffering but reigning from the tree. Above his head the Hand of God emerges from a cloud. Though weathered, the figure keeps the calm majesty of late Anglo-Saxon art, which drew on manuscript models of the Winchester school.
facts: The Web Gallery of Art dates it 1000–1020 and notes that it translates into stone models from Winchester-school manuscripts.
Christ is shown upright, head held erect and arms outstretched in welcome, with the Hand of God emerging from the clouds above him.
It may originally have stood inside the earlier Saxon church and been reset on the Norman building, where a modern canopy now shelters it.
wga:m/master/yunk_en/00cross.notes: Dating varies (first half of the 11th century; Talbot Rice 1000–20; some link it to the church of 967).
